rules.statement: Rotate the refresh token of a public client on every refresh unless the grant is sender-constrained by a stored proof-of-possession confirmation (DPoP `jkt` or certificate `x5t#S256`), and do not let any setting or option turn that rotation off.
rules.why: RFC 9700 §2.2.2/§4.14.2 and OAuth 2.1 §4.3.1 require a public client's refresh token to be either sender-constrained or rotated; otherwise the client gets a reusable bearer refresh token.
rules.check: Look for refresh-token grant logic or settings where a public (non-confidential) client without a token confirmation can keep its refresh token, e.g. a boolean rotation flag that defaults to false or that can override the requirement.

rules.statement: Do not rotate, by default, the refresh token of a confidential client whose tokens are sender-constrained; decide whether to rotate from the binding of each token, not by forcing rotation for every client.
rules.why: FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.1 forbids rotation for sender-constrained confidential clients: it adds no security there, and a client that loses the rotation response loses its session.
rules.check: Look for defaults or profiles that rotate every refresh token (an 'always' policy) for confidential or DPoP/mTLS-bound clients, or for rotation decisions made only from the client registration and not from the token's confirmation.

rules.statement: Validate a setting whose value selects a behavior the server enforces against a closed set of allowed values, and reject (fail closed on) any unknown value.
rules.why: An unknown value for an enforced security behavior must not silently fall through to a weaker behavior.
rules.check: Look for new policy-style string settings that accept arbitrary values or fall back to a default on unrecognized input, instead of using a one-of validation that rejects them.

rules.statement: A data migration that rewrites stored JSON documents must rewrite a document only when it is a JSON object, the old key has the expected type, and the target key is absent, and it must give every rewritten row a new concurrency token.
rules.why: Guarded rewrites avoid corrupting unexpected or already-migrated data, and a new concurrency token makes cached or concurrent writers notice that the row changed.
rules.check: Look for migrations that rewrite JSON columns without checking the document shape, the old value's type, or an existing target key, or that update rows without regenerating the concurrency token.
